Winners of the UK Best Places To Work Awards 2026 revealed | GamesIndustry.biz

The UK Best Places to Work Awards 2026 took place at the Royal Institution in London on October 1, with special awards going to Dink, Hangar 13, Jagex: The RuneScape Company, NaturalMotion Games, Rare, and Snap Finger Click.
The awards ceremony took place after the GamesIndustry.biz HR Summit, which was attended by 79 representatives from 41 companies, including AAA, AA, and indie studios, as well as consultancy firms, training providers, and educational institutes.
The main Best Places to Work awards recognised a total of 25 firms across three categories – small, mid-sized, and large companies – for their excellence in supporting staff. These awards are judged on the basis of an employee survey (worth 80% of the score) and a company survey (worth 20%).
The Best Places to Work Awards 2026 was sponsored by Amiqus, Playground Games, IO Interactive, Games London, and Special Effect.
“What makes these events especially valuable is how well they complement each other," said Liz Prince MBE, Business Manager at Amiqus. "The HR Summit creates space for honest discussions, shared learning and new ideas, while the Best Places To Work Awards shine a spotlight on the studios and businesses that are turning those ideas into action. Bringing the industry together to both learn from each other and celebrate success helps raise standards for everyone, and we're proud to play a part in that.”
“We’re proud to support GI.Biz in recognising the UK’s best mid-sized Video Game Studios," said Paul Evans, Director of HR & Recruitment at Playground Games. "These are not only teams that are creating brilliant games, but studios who are also setting the standard for what a great place to work looks like in our industry”.

The winner of this year's G Into Gaming award was Jo Haslam, currently Design Director at Snap Finger Click following a long career at Mediatonic, Relentless and the BBC. Liz Prince MBE presented the award, describing Haslam as "one of those rare people who leads with both empathy and action in perfect unison," and "an inspiring woman and a natural leader." Snap Finger Click also left with both a Best Places to Work Award and this year's Diversity Award.
Rare once again took the Environmental Award, sponsored by Games London, while Middlesborough indie Dink won the Education Award, presented by IO Interactive Chief Development Officer Veronique Lallier.
